q: Cells divide on a regular basic to bring about growth and asexual reproduction.
e: True. Cells divide on a regular basic to bring about growth and asexual reproduction. Asexual reproduction copies one parent, often through mitosis.

q: Cells divide on a regular basic to bring about growth and sexual reproduction.
e: False. Ordinary cell division supports growth and asexual reproduction. Sexual reproduction needs meiosis and gametes.

q: Interphase is a period of non-division, which is subdivided into $G_1$, S and $G_2$ stages.
e: True. Interphase is a period of non-division, which is subdivided into G1, S and G2 stages. S is the synthesis stage of interphase when DNA is copied. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA.

q: Interphase is a period of active division, which is subdivided into $G_1$, S and $G_2$ stages.
e: False. Interphase is a non-division growth period. Nuclear division happens in mitosis, not in interphase.

q: In $G_1$ stage, the growth of cell takes place.
e: True. In G1 stage, the growth of cell takes place.

q: In $G_1$ stage, DNA replication is carried out.
e: False. G1 is for cell growth. DNA is copied in S phase, not in G1.

q: DNA replication is carried out in S stage.
e: True. DNA replication is carried out in S stage. DNA replication happens in S phase. DNA is replicated in S phase of interphase.

q: After replication is completed, each chromosome consists of four identical DNA molecules called chromatids.
e: False. It is not true that after replication is completed, each chromosome consists of four identical DNA molecules called chromatids. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: Chromatids are joined together at a point called the centromere.
e: True. Chromatids are joined together at a point called the centromere. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach.

q: Chromatids are joined together at a point called the centrosome.
e: False. It is not true that chromatids are joined together at a point called the centrosome. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: In $G_2$ stage, the organelles are replicated and the cell grows.
e: True. In G2 stage, the organelles are replicated and the cell grows.

q: Mitosis is a period of active nuclear division and cytokinesis is the separation of cytoplasm.
e: True. Mitosis is a period of active nuclear division and cytokinesis is the separation of cytoplasm. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus.

q: Mitosis is a period of active cytoplasmic division and cytokinesis is the separation of the nucleus.
e: False. Mitosis is a period of active cytoplasmic division and cytokinesis is not the separation of the nucleus. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Mitosis divides the nucleus so two daughter nuclei get identical chromosomes.

q: Cell division is a strictly regulated process that mostly works without errors.
e: True. Cell division is a strictly regulated process that mostly works without errors.

q: When errors do occur in cell division, they can be catastrophic and cause the development of cancer.
e: True. When errors do occur in cell division, they can be catastrophic and cause the development of cancer. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division after control checkpoints fail.

q: The interphase, the initial stage of the cell cycle, used to be called the resting phase.
e: True. The interphase, the initial stage of the cell cycle, used to be called the resting phase. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. The cell cycle is the ordered sequence of growth, DNA copy, and division.

q: During interphase, the normal metabolic processes of the cell stop and no new DNA is produced.
e: False. It is not true that during interphase, the normal metabolic processes of the cell stop and no new DNA is produced. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: During mitosis, the chromosomes that are duplicated during interphase are divided to produce two identical daughter cells.
e: True. During mitosis, the chromosomes that are duplicated during interphase are divided to produce two identical daughter cells. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: Mitosis is divided into four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase.
e: True. Mitosis is divided into four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. In metaphase chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate. In telophase nuclei reform around the two chromosome sets.

q: During prophase, the chromatins become more tightly coiled and condensing into discrete chromosomes.
e: True. During prophase, the chromatins become more tightly coiled and condensing into discrete chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle starts to form.

q: During prophase, the nuclear envelope forms and the nucleolus appears.
e: False. It is not true that during prophase, the nuclear envelope forms and the nucleolus appears. The nuclear envelope breaks down in prophase and reforms in telophase. The nucleolus vanishes in prophase and returns in telophase.

q: The radial arrays of shorter microtubules around each centriole are called asters.
e: True. The radial arrays of shorter microtubules around each centriole are called asters. Asters are microtubule arrays around the poles in animal mitosis.

q: During metaphase, the chromosomes line up along the metaphase plate (equator) of the cell.
e: True. During metaphase, the chromosomes line up along the metaphase plate (equator) of the cell. The metaphase plate is the equator where chromosomes align. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: During metaphase, each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its telomere.
e: False. It is not true that during metaphase, each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its telomere. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. In metaphase chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate.

q: During anaphase, the chromatids from each pair are pulled, centromere first, towards opposite poles of the cell.
e: True. During anaphase, the chromatids from each pair are pulled, centromere first, towards opposite poles of the cell. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach.

q: During anaphase, the centromeres do not divide and sister chromatids remain attached.
e: False. It is not true that during anaphase, the centromeres do not divide and sister chromatids remain attached. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

q: At the end of anaphase, the chromatids are now called chromosomes, as each is an identical copy of chromosome.
e: True. At the end of anaphase, the chromatids are now called chromosomes, as each is an identical copy of chromosome. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: During telophase, the spindle fibres break down and nuclear envelopes reform around the two sets of chromosomes.
e: True. During telophase, the spindle fibres break down and nuclear envelopes reform around the two sets of chromosomes. Two nuclear envelopes form in telophase. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: During telophase, the chromosomes begin to coil and becoming more dense.
e: False. It is not true that during telophase, the chromosomes begin to coil and becoming more dense. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. In telophase nuclei reform around the two chromosome sets.

q: The final phase of the cell cycle is cytokinesis, when the cytoplasm divides.
e: True. The final phase of the cell cycle is cytokinesis, when the cytoplasm divides. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. Many metabolic reactions run in the cytoplasm.

q: In animal cells, a cellulose cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards during cytokinesis.
e: False. It is not true that in animal cells, a cellulose cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards during cytokinesis. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid.

q: In plant cells, a cellulose cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards during cytokinesis.
e: True. In plant cells, a cellulose cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards during cytokinesis. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid.

q: Meiosis is a type of nuclear division that happens only in sex organs.
e: True. Meiosis is a type of nuclear division that happens only in sex organs. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Meiosis is called reduction division because the cells that are formed have half the number of chromosomes.
e: True. Meiosis is called reduction division because the cells that are formed have half the number of chromosomes. Meiosis I is the reduction division that halves chromosome number. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: In animals, the somatic cells are formed directly from meiosis.
e: False. It is not true that in animals, the somatic cells are formed directly from meiosis. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: The formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis, while that of ovum is called oogenesis.
e: True. The formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis, while that of ovum is called oogenesis. Spermatogenesis is meiosis that produces sperm. Oogenesis is meiosis that produces eggs.

q: In flowering plants, meiosis forms special male cells called microspores and female cells called megaspores.
e: True. In flowering plants, meiosis forms special male cells called microspores and female cells called megaspores. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: In meiosis, two nuclear divisions produce four haploid daughter cells, each with its own unique combination of genetic material.
e: True. In meiosis, two nuclear divisions produce four haploid daughter cells, each with its own unique combination of genetic material. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: During prophase I of meiosis, homologous pairs of chromosomes pair along their lengths which is called synapsis.
e: True. During prophase I of meiosis, homologous pairs of chromosomes pair along their lengths which is called synapsis. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle starts to form.

q: During prophase I of meiosis, crossing over occurs between sister chromatids.
e: False. It is not true that during prophase I of meiosis, crossing over occurs between sister chromatids. Crossing over in prophase I swaps DNA between homologous chromosomes. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: During metaphase I, homologous pairs of chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate.
e: True. During metaphase I, homologous pairs of chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate. The metaphase plate is the equator where chromosomes align. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: During anaphase I, the centromeres divide and sister chromatids separate.
e: False. It is not true that during anaphase I, the centromeres divide and sister chromatids separate. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

q: No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II.
e: True. No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II. Meiosis halves the chromosome number for gametes. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: In prophase I of meiosis, crossing over introduces genetic variation as the chromatids may break and recombine.
e: True. In prophase I of meiosis, crossing over introduces genetic variation as the chromatids may break and recombine. Meiosis, crossing over, and random fertilisation generate genetic variation. Crossing over in prophase I swaps DNA between homologous chromosomes.
